```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r model-load, include = FALSE}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Fouad_2024_cefiderocol"))
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/ofid/ofae451> (PMC11492798; open access,
  CC BY)
* Supplement: Tables S1-S3 (eligibility, the label's CRRT dosing table and the
  per-patient actual-versus-label exposure comparison) and Figures S1-S2
  (covariate regressions and individual fits)

Cefiderocol is a siderophore cephalosporin whose United States label was the
first to give antibiotic dosing by continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT)
effluent flow rate: 1.5 g q12h, 2 g q12h, 1.5 g q8h and 2 g q8h, each as a
3 h infusion, for effluent flows of at most 2, 2.1-3, 3.1-4 and at least
4.1 L/h. Fouad and colleagues ran a prospective three-centre study in
critically ill adults on CRRT to validate those bands, fitting prefilter
plasma concentrations nonparametrically with the NPAG algorithm in Pmetrics.
The two-compartment base model they selected is the model packaged here.

# Population

Fourteen ICU patients on continuous venovenous haemodiafiltration (CVVHDF,
Prismaflex) were enrolled between August 2022 and December 2023 at Hartford
Hospital (n = 7), Banner-University Medical Center (n = 5) and the University
of Kentucky (n = 2). Five received cefiderocol for an actual or suspected
infection and nine for PK sampling only. Five were dosed according to the
label's effluent-flow bands; nine had doses adjusted by the clinical team for
obesity, residual renal function or an effluent flow that moved between bands
(Supplementary Table S3). Prefilter samples were drawn after at least two prior
doses at 0, 1.5, 3, 4, 6, 8 and (for q12h regimens) 12 h after the start of the
dose.

# Typical-value simulation of the label regimens

The four label regimens are simulated for four days of dosing, at which point
the system is at steady state (terminal half-life about 5.5 h at the typical
values), and the final dosing interval is analysed. `FU` is set to the cohort
mean of 0.84, since per-patient values are not published.

```{r regimens}
regimens <- data.frame(
  regimen = c("1.5 g q12h", "2 g q12h", "1.5 g q8h", "2 g q8h"),
  band    = c("<= 2 L/h", "2.1-3 L/h", "3.1-4 L/h", ">= 4.1 L/h"),
  amt     = c(1500, 2000, 1500, 2000),
  tau     = c(12, 12, 8, 8),
  # Number of study patients in each effluent band (Table 1).
  n_paper = c(1, 4, 7, 2)
)
regimens$daily_dose <- regimens$amt * 24 / regimens$tau
TEND <- 96
DUR  <- 3
FU_MEAN <- 0.84

mkEvents <- function(ids, reg, grid = 0.1) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(ids), function(i) {
    r <- regimens[reg[i], ]
    dose_times <- seq(0, TEND - r$tau, by = r$tau)
    dos <- data.frame(
      id = ids[i], time = dose_times, amt = r$amt, rate = r$amt / DUR,
      evid = 1, cmt = "central"
    )
    obs <- data.frame(
      id = ids[i], time = seq(TEND - r$tau, TEND, by = grid), amt = 0,
      rate = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central"
    )
    out <- rbind(dos, obs)
    out$regimen <- r$regimen
    out$FU <- FU_MEAN
    out[order(out$time, -out$evid), ]
  }))
}

mod_tv <- rxode2::zeroRe(ui)
ev_tv <- mkEvents(1:4, 1:4)
# Four typical-value subjects, one per regimen; rxode2 warns that a
# multi-subject solve has no omega, which is the intent here.
sim_tv <- suppressWarnings(as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_tv, events = ev_tv, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame"
)))
```

## Structural check: the peripheral compartment is solved

AUC over a dosing interval at steady state equals dose/CL for any linear
model, so an AUC check cannot tell a two-compartment solve from a collapsed
one-compartment one. The terminal slope can: after a single dose it must equal
the slow disposition rate `beta` of the micro-constants.

```{r structural-gate}
th <- exp(ui$theta[c("lcl", "lvc", "lk12", "lk21")])
k10 <- th[["lcl"]] / th[["lvc"]]
k12 <- th[["lk12"]]
k21 <- th[["lk21"]]
ssum <- k10 + k12 + k21
beta <- (ssum - sqrt(ssum^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2

ev_sd <- data.frame(
  id = 1, time = c(0, seq(20, 40, by = 1)), amt = c(2000, rep(0, 21)),
  rate = c(2000 / DUR, rep(0, 21)), evid = c(1, rep(0, 21)),
  cmt = "central", FU = FU_MEAN
)
sd_tv <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_tv, events = ev_sd))
slope <- -coef(lm(log(Cc) ~ time, data = sd_tv))[["time"]]
sprintf(
  "terminal slope %.5f 1/h vs closed-form beta %.5f 1/h (half-life %.2f h)",
  slope, beta, log(2) / beta
)
stopifnot(
  "peripheral1" %in% names(sd_tv),
  # Both sides use the same parameters, and by 20 h the alpha phase
  # (rate ~5.3 1/h) has decayed by more than e^-80, so the difference is
  # integrator error only (realised ~3e-6 relative).
  abs(slope - beta) / beta < 1e-3
)
```

```{r tv-profile, fig.cap = "Typical-value steady-state total (solid) and free (dashed) cefiderocol over the final dosing interval for each label regimen."}
sim_tv %>%
  dplyr::left_join(regimens[, c("regimen", "tau")], by = "regimen") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    tad = time - (TEND - tau),
    regimen = factor(regimen, levels = regimens$regimen)
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cfree), names_to = "measure", values_to = "conc") %>%
  ggplot(aes(tad, conc, colour = regimen, linetype = measure)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of infusion (h)",
    y = "Cefiderocol (mg/L)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## PKNCA against the closed form

```{r pknca-tv}
nca_conc_tv <- sim_tv %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) %>%
  dplyr::select(id, regimen, time, Cc)
nca_dose_tv <- ev_tv %>%
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) %>%
  dplyr::select(id, regimen, time, amt)
int_tv <- regimens %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    regimen, start = TEND - tau, end = TEND,
    auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE
  )
nca_tv <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc_tv, Cc ~ time | regimen + id,
                   concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h"),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose_tv, amt ~ time | regimen + id,
                   doseu = "mg", duration = DUR),
  intervals = int_tv
)))

tv_chk <- nca_tv %>%
  dplyr::select(regimen, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(regimens, by = "regimen") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc_daily = auclast * 24 / tau,
    closed_form = daily_dose / th[["lcl"]],
    pct = 100 * (auc_daily - closed_form) / closed_form
  )
tv_chk %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    regimen, band, cmax, cmin, auc_daily, closed_form, pct
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen, "Effluent band" = band,
    "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "Ctrough (mg/L)" = cmin,
    "AUCdaily, PKNCA (mg*h/L)" = auc_daily,
    "Daily dose / CL (mg*h/L)" = closed_form, "% diff" = pct
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical patient at steady state.")
# Trapezoidal AUC on a 0.1 h grid against the exact integral; realised error
# is about 0.003%.
stopifnot(nrow(tv_chk) == 4L, max(abs(tv_chk$pct)) < 0.1)
```

# Mean or median as the typical value

Table 2 reports each parameter's mean +/- SD and median. The paper's own
exposure summary, the pooled AUCdaily of 1444 +/- 423 mg*h/L (Results) with a
median of about 1430 and an interquartile range of about 1290-1720 mg*h/L
(digitised from the CRRT box of Figure 2), depends only on the clearance
distribution and the label dose of each patient's effluent band, because
AUCdaily is the daily dose divided by clearance. With a lognormal clearance it
can therefore be computed exactly, without simulation, for either choice of
typical value. The patients are weighted by the Table 1 effluent bands.

```{r mean-vs-median}
w  <- regimens$n_paper / sum(regimens$n_paper)
DD <- regimens$daily_dose
om_cl <- ui$omega["etalcl", "etalcl"]

aucDist <- function(tvcl) {
  mu <- log(tvcl)
  cdf <- function(a) sum(w * (1 - plnorm(DD / a, mu, sqrt(om_cl))))
  q <- vapply(
    c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
    function(p) uniroot(function(a) cdf(a) - p, c(10, 1e5))$root,
    numeric(1)
  )
  c(mean = sum(w * DD) * exp(-mu + om_cl / 2), q1 = q[1], median = q[2], q3 = q[3])
}
published <- c(mean = 1444, q1 = 1290, median = 1430, q3 = 1720)
mm <- rbind(
  Published = published,
  `Median column (CL 3.3)` = aucDist(3.3),
  `Mean column (CL 3.5)` = aucDist(3.5)
)
knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame(mm) %>%
    dplyr::rename(
      "Mean AUCdaily" = mean, "Q1" = q1, "Median" = median, "Q3" = q3
    ),
  digits = 0,
  caption = paste(
    "Pooled AUCdaily (mg*h/L) under label dosing. Published mean from the",
    "Results; quartiles digitised from Figure 2."
  )
)
stopifnot(
  # Deterministic. The median column gives +1.5% on the mean and -6.7% on the
  # median; the mean column gives -4.3% and -12%.
  abs(mm[2, "mean"] / 1444 - 1) < 0.03,
  abs(mm[2, "median"] / 1430 - 1) < abs(mm[3, "median"] / 1430 - 1)
)
```

The median column lands closer on both the mean and the median, and it is also
the reading under which Table 2 is internally consistent: a lognormal with the
printed median and the SD-derived variance has a mean of 3.58 L/h for CL,
3.85 1/h for k12 and 2.12 1/h for k21, against the printed means of 3.5, 3.9
and 2.2. The model therefore encodes the medians.

The modelled interquartile range is wider than the published one (Q1 997
against about 1290). The study dosed by effluent band, and effluent flow was
correlated with clearance (Supplementary Figure S1), so the bands partly
cancelled the between-patient spread in clearance. The final model carries no
effluent covariate, so the simulation assigns doses independently of
clearance, and that link is lost.

# Stochastic cohort under label dosing

A virtual cohort of 280 patients is split across the four effluent bands in the
Table 1 proportions (20 per study patient: 20, 80, 140 and 40), so no arm
exceeds 200.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241015)
n_arm <- regimens$n_paper * 20
reg_id <- rep(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), n_arm)
ev_vpc <- mkEvents(seq_along(reg_id), reg_id, grid = 0.25)
sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  ui, events = ev_vpc, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame"
))
sim <- dplyr::left_join(sim, regimens[, c("regimen", "tau")], by = "regimen")
```

```{r vpc, fig.cap = "Steady-state total cefiderocol over the final dosing interval by label regimen: median and 5th-95th percentiles of the virtual cohort."}
sim %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    tad = time - (TEND - tau),
    regimen = factor(regimen, levels = regimens$regimen)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, tad) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), med = median(Cc), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(tad, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after start of infusion (h)", y = "Total cefiderocol (mg/L)") +
  theme_bw()
```

## PKNCA: pooled AUCdaily

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) %>%
  dplyr::select(id, regimen, time, Cc)
nca_dose <- ev_vpc %>%
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) %>%
  dplyr::select(id, regimen, time, amt)
nca_res <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | regimen + id,
                   concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h"),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | regimen + id,
                   doseu = "mg", duration = DUR),
  intervals = int_tv
)))

auc_daily <- nca_res %>%
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(regimens[, c("regimen", "tau")], by = "regimen") %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    id, regimen, PPTESTCD = "auclast", PPORRES = PPORRES * 24 / tau
  )
stopifnot(nrow(auc_daily) == sum(n_arm))

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  auc_daily, data.frame(auclast = 1430),
  params = "auclast",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L, AUCdaily = AUCtau x 24 / tau")
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Pooled median AUCdaily against the CRRT median digitised from Fouad 2024",
    "Figure 2.", attr(cmp, "footnote")
  )
)
sprintf(
  "simulated pooled AUCdaily: mean %.0f, SD %.0f, median %.0f (published mean 1444 +/- 423)",
  mean(auc_daily$PPORRES), sd(auc_daily$PPORRES), median(auc_daily$PPORRES)
)
stopifnot(
  # Exact model value is 1334 (deterministic chunk above); a mis-transcribed
  # clearance or dose moves it by tens of percent. 280 patients put the
  # Monte Carlo SE of the median near 3%.
  abs(median(auc_daily$PPORRES) / 1430 - 1) < 0.2
)
```

```{r auc-figure, fig.cap = "Replicates the CRRT box of Fouad 2024 Figure 2: AUCdaily under label dosing. Box = interquartile range, whiskers = minimum and maximum. The grey box is the published one (digitised); the simulated box pools the four effluent bands."}
pub_box <- data.frame(
  source = "Published (n = 14)", ymin = 644, lower = 1290, middle = 1430,
  upper = 1720, ymax = 2156
)
sim_box <- auc_daily %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    ymin = min(PPORRES), lower = quantile(PPORRES, 0.25),
    middle = median(PPORRES), upper = quantile(PPORRES, 0.75),
    ymax = max(PPORRES)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(source = "Simulated (n = 280)")
ggplot(rbind(pub_box, sim_box[, names(pub_box)]), aes(x = source)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    aes(ymin = ymin, lower = lower, middle = middle, upper = upper, ymax = ymax,
        fill = source),
    stat = "identity", width = 0.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey70", "steelblue"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "AUCdaily (mg*h/L)") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Free time above the MIC

Table 3 gives each patient's %fT > MIC under the label dose for their effluent
band. Below, the share of patients reaching 100% and at least 75% fT > MIC
(the clinical-success target) is compared with the share of the virtual
cohort.

```{r ftmic}
mics <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32)
sim_last <- dplyr::filter(sim, time > TEND - tau)
ft_mat <- vapply(
  mics,
  function(m) 100 * tapply(sim_last$Cfree > m, sim_last$id, mean),
  numeric(length(unique(sim_last$id)))
)

# Fouad 2024 Table 3, patients 1-14; MICs 0.5-8 mg/L are 100% for everyone.
ft_pub <- cbind(
  matrix(100, nrow = 14, ncol = 5),
  c(100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 82, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100),
  c(94, 100, 92, 75, 100, 86, 94, 0, 49, 100, 100, 99, 100, 6)
)
stopifnot(nrow(ft_mat) == sum(n_arm), ncol(ft_mat) == length(mics))

ftmic <- data.frame(
  MIC = mics,
  pub100 = 100 * colMeans(ft_pub >= 100),
  sim100 = 100 * colMeans(ft_mat >= 100),
  pub75 = 100 * colMeans(ft_pub >= 75),
  sim75 = 100 * colMeans(ft_mat >= 75)
)
ftmic %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    "MIC (mg/L)" = MIC,
    "100% fT>MIC, published (%)" = pub100,
    "100% fT>MIC, simulated (%)" = sim100,
    ">= 75% fT>MIC, published (%)" = pub75,
    ">= 75% fT>MIC, simulated (%)" = sim75
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Share of patients reaching the target.")
stopifnot(
  # The paper's headline claim is that every patient reaches 100% fT > MIC up
  # to 8 mg/L under label dosing. At the 4 mg/L susceptible breakpoint the
  # virtual cohort reaches the 75% target in about 98% of patients and 100%
  # fT > MIC in about 92%; these bounds are set well inside those values
  # because they are shares of a random cohort's tail.
  ftmic$sim75[ftmic$MIC == 4] > 90,
  ftmic$sim100[ftmic$MIC == 4] > 80
)
```

All 14 study patients reached 100% fT > MIC up to 8 mg/L. The virtual cohort
reaches the clinical 75% target in at least 93% of patients up to 8 mg/L, but
100% fT > MIC in fewer of them (about 92% at 4 mg/L and 87% at 8 mg/L). At
32 mg/L the share reaching 100% is close to the paper's (5 of 14), while the
share reaching 75% is lower (11 of 14 in the paper). The shortfall sits in the
low tail of the trough distribution, which is set by the wide spread of k21 and
Vc (CVs of 100% and 79%) and by the clearance-dose link discussed above. A
lognormal with independent etas puts more weight in that tail than the 14
individual posterior estimates did, so the model is conservative for target
attainment at the upper MICs.

# Individual clearances recovered from Table S3

Table S3 gives, for each of the nine patients dosed off-label, the AUCdaily of
both the actual and the label regimen. Since AUCdaily is daily dose divided by
the individual Bayesian clearance, both rows return the same clearance, which
checks the transcription and places nine of the 14 individual clearances
against the model's distribution.

```{r table-s3}
s3 <- data.frame(
  patient = c(2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 13, 14),
  effluent = c(2.08, 2.14, 3.67, 3.41, 4.77, 3.34, 5.06, 3.02, 3.15),
  dd_actual = c(3000, 4000, 8000, 8000, 8000, 6000, 8000, 8000, 4000),
  auc_actual = c(1617, 1966, 2494, 2482, 2086, 859, 1376, 1628, 1182),
  dd_label = c(4000, 3000, 4500, 4500, 6000, 4500, 6000, 4000, 4500),
  auc_label = c(2156, 1474, 1403, 1396, 1565, 644, 1032, 814, 1329)
)
s3 <- s3 %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    cl_actual = dd_actual / auc_actual,
    cl_label = dd_label / auc_label,
    pct_model = 100 * plnorm(cl_actual, log(th[["lcl"]]), sqrt(om_cl))
  )
s3 %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    "Patient" = patient, "Effluent (L/h)" = effluent,
    "CL from actual regimen (L/h)" = cl_actual,
    "CL from label regimen (L/h)" = cl_label,
    "Percentile of model CL" = pct_model
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-dd_actual, -auc_actual, -dd_label, -auc_label) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  # AUCs are printed to the nearest mg*h/L, so the two clearances agree to
  # rounding (realised max 0.06%).
  max(abs(s3$cl_actual / s3$cl_label - 1)) < 0.005
)
```

All nine fall between the 7th and 97th percentiles of the model's clearance
distribution. Clearance rises with effluent flow among them (patients 2 and 3
at about 2.1 L/h have the two lowest clearances), which is the correlation the
authors report in Supplementary Figure S1 but did not retain in the model.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Median column as the typical value.** Table 2 gives mean +/- SD and
  median. The medians are encoded as lognormal medians and the SDs become
  lognormal variances via `omega^2 = log(1 + (SD/mean)^2)`. The choice is
  supported by the closed-form AUCdaily comparison above and by the internal
  consistency of Table 2 under a lognormal; for Vc the lognormal mean (9.4 L)
  is below the printed mean (10.7 L), reflecting a right tail heavier than
  lognormal in the NPAG density.
* **Independent etas.** No covariance or correlation matrix of the
  nonparametric joint density is published, so the four etas are independent.
  The shape of the NPAG density, including any multimodality, cannot be
  recovered from Table 2.
* **Residual error.** The Pmetrics assay polynomial `0.006 + 0.06 * C` is
  multiplied by the published fitted gamma of 1.6 and encoded as
  `combined1()`, since Pmetrics sums the additive and proportional parts
  linearly. Pmetrics evaluates the polynomial at the observed concentration;
  nlmixr2 evaluates it at the prediction.
* **No covariates on disposition.** Body weight, effluent flow and
  transmembrane clearance correlated with individual clearance but did not
  improve AIC and are not in the final model; they are documented in
  `covariatesDataExcluded`. Simulations by effluent band therefore draw
  clearance independently of the band, which widens the modelled AUCdaily
  distribution relative to the study's.
* **Fraction unbound.** `Cfree = FU * Cc` uses the measured per-patient
  fraction unbound as a covariate. Per-patient values are not published; the
  simulations use the cohort mean 0.84. Typical non-critically ill binding is
  40-60%, so FU around 0.5 is the appropriate input outside this population.
* **Figure 2 values** (median 1430, quartiles 1290 and 1720, whiskers 644 and
  2156 mg*h/L) were digitised by the maintainers from the published figure;
  the whiskers coincide with the Table S3 label-regimen extremes (patient 8:
  644, patient 2: 2156), which anchors the digitisation.
* **Population.** All patients were on CVVHDF with effluent flows of
  2.08-5.1 L/h. The model is not informed by other CRRT modalities, by
  intermittent dialysis, or by effluent flows outside that range, and residual
  renal function was present in some patients but not modelled.

# Errata and provenance notes

* Table 2 prints the CL SD as 1.46 L/h; the Abstract rounds it to 1.5. The
  Table 2 value is used.
* No erratum or correction to this article was found on Europe PMC
  (checked 2026-10-30).
* The same group's sibling model in people with cystic fibrosis is
  `Koenig_2025_cefiderocol`, which has the same CL / Vc / k12 / k21
  parameterisation. The CRRT clearance here (3.3 L/h) is lower than that
  cohort's (5.66 L/h, normal-to-augmented renal function) and the
  fraction unbound is higher (0.84 against 0.52).
